content: **SPECIAL TESTS LUMBO SACRAL REGION** --- **I TEST FOR LUMBAR INSTABILITY** --- **1 PASSIVE LUMBAR EXTENSION TEST** PURPOSE To assess lumbar spine instability PROCEDURE • Patient lies prone • Examiner lifts both the patients legs together by holding around the ankles • The legs are elevated while the knees remain extended • Observe the patients symptoms and lumbar response POSITIVE SIGN • Development/reproduction of low back pain • Feeling of heaviness or instability in the lumbar region INDICATES Lumbar segmental instability --- **II TESTS FOR MUSCLE DYSFUNCTION** --- **2 90 90 STRAIGHT LEG RAISING TEST** PURPOSE To assess hamstring muscle tightness/flexibility PROCEDURE • Patient lies supine • Flex the hip and knee to approximately 90 • Stabilize the thigh • Slowly extend the knee while maintaining hip flexion POSITIVE SIGN • Inability to achieve full knee extension • Increased resistance/tightness in the posterior thigh INDICATES Hamstring tightness/shortness --- **3 TRENDELENBURG TEST** PURPOSE To assess hip abductor muscle function especially gluteus medius PROCEDURE • Patient stands on one leg • Ask the patient to lift the opposite foot from the floor • Observe the position of the pelvis POSITIVE SIGN • Pelvis drops on the side of the lifted/non weight bearing leg INDICATES Weakness of the hip abductors of the weight bearing leg particularly gluteus medius --- **III TESTS FOR NEUROLOGICAL DYSFUNCTION** --- **4 STRAIGHT LEG RAISING TEST SLR/LASÈGUES TEST** PURPOSE To assess lumbosacral nerve root irritation particularly due to PIVD PROCEDURE • Patient lies supine • Keep the knee fully extended • Slowly raise the patients straight leg by flexing the hip • Note the angle and symptoms produced POSITIVE SIGN • Reproduction of radicular/sciatic pain typically between about 30 70 of hip flexion INDICATES Lumbosacral nerve root irritation/compression commonly associated with PIVD --- **5 SLUMP TEST** PURPOSE To assess neural tissue mechanosensitivity particularly lumbosacral nerve root involvement PROCEDURE Patient sits with 1 Hands behind back 2 Thoracic/lumbar spine flexed 3 Cervical spine flexed 4 One knee is extended 5 Ankle is dorsiflexed The examiner progressively adds these components while observing symptoms POSITIVE SIGN • Reproduction of the patients familiar neural/radicular symptoms • Symptoms change with release of one component particularly cervical extension or ankle movement INDICATES Neural tissue/nerve root involvement such as lumbar radiculopathy --- **IV TESTS FOR JOINT DYSFUNCTION** --- **6 SCHOBERS TEST** PURPOSE To assess lumbar spine flexion/mobility PROCEDURE • Patient stands erect • Mark the lumbosacral region and a point 10 cm above it • Ask the patient to bend forward maximally • Measure the distance between the marks again POSITIVE SIGN Insufficient increase in distance during forward flexion INDICATES Reduced lumbar flexion/mobility commonly seen in conditions such as ankylosing spondylitis --- **7 FABER / PATRICKS TEST** FABER Flexion ABduction External Rotation PURPOSE To assess hip and sacroiliac joint pathology PROCEDURE • Patient lies supine • Place the tested leg in • Hip flexion • Abduction • External rotation • Place the lateral ankle over the opposite thigh • Stabilize the opposite pelvis • Gently press the flexed knee downward POSITIVE SIGN • Pain reproduced in the hip/groin suggests hip pathology • Pain in the sacroiliac region may indicate SI joint pathology • Restricted ROM may also be significant INDICATES Hip or sacroiliac joint dysfunction --- **8 GAENSLENS TEST** PURPOSE To assess sacroiliac joint dysfunction/pathology PROCEDURE • Patient lies near the edge of the table • One hip and knee are maximally flexed toward the chest • The opposite leg is allowed to hang off the edge of the table • Apply gentle pressure to produce opposite movements at the pelvis POSITIVE SIGN • Reproduction of pain in the sacroiliac region INDICATES Sacroiliac joint dysfunction --- **9 GILLETS TEST** PURPOSE To assess sacroiliac joint mobility PROCEDURE • Patient stands • Examiner palpates the PSIS and sacrum • Patient flexes one hip and knee lifting the foot from the floor • Observe movement of the PSIS relative to the sacrum POSITIVE SIGN • Abnormal or restricted movement of the PSIS compared with the opposite side INDICATES Sacroiliac joint hypomobility/dysfunction --- **10 MARCHS TEST** PURPOSE To assess sacroiliac joint movement/dysfunction PROCEDURE • Patient stands • Examiner palpates the PSIS • Patient marches by lifting one knee at a time • Observe the movement of the PSIS POSITIVE SIGN • Abnormal/asymmetrical movement of the PSIS INDICATES Sacroiliac joint dysfunction or altered mobility
